questions.question:
D1 — Which implementation approach should this plan use? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-approach-selection>

ELI10: The plan introduces a new Stripe webhook handler that reads a user ID from Stripe event metadata into a raw SQL query — and the plan itself explicitly says this is unsafe SQL. There are also no tests, and email errors propagate silently after the payment is committed. We have three paths: ship it as-is (fast, insecure), fix just the SQL (quick win), or fix all three known issues (secure, tested, reliable).

Stakes if we pick wrong: Approach A ships a handler with a named SQL injection vulnerability the plan's own text acknowledges. Approach B leaves a reliability gap where email errors cause misleading HTTP 500s after committed payments.

Recommendation: C because the SQL injection is P0, the email fix is one rescue clause, and the test suite is ~20 min with CC — deferring all three accepts known risk for no real benefit.

Completeness: A=3/10, B=6/10, C=9/10

Pros/cons:
A) As-specified — raw SQL, no tests, no email rescue
  ✅ Smallest possible diff; matches the plan document exactly as written
  ❌ Ships a SQL injection the plan itself calls out as unsafe; no test coverage means no regression baseline

B) Minimal safe — parameterize the SQL query only
  ✅ Eliminates the P0 SQL injection with minimal code change; everything else stays the same
  ❌ Email exceptions still propagate after DB commits (misleading HTTP 500, no auto-retry for the notification); still no tests

C) Full fix — parameterized queries + email rescue + unit tests (recommended)
  ✅ Eliminates SQL injection; email failures no longer misrepresent committed payments; tests create a regression baseline for future changes
  ❌ More code to write; requires existing test harness to support the new handler class

Net: trading ~15 extra CC minutes for a handler that doesn't ship with a named security vulnerability and has a test baseline.

options.label: A) As-specified (raw SQL)
options.description: Implement exactly as written — raw SQL fragment, no email rescue, no tests. Fast but ships the acknowledged SQL injection.

options.label: B) Minimal safe (parameterize only)
options.description: Fix the SQL injection with parameterized queries; keep email inline with no rescue and no tests.

options.label: C) Full fix — all three gaps (Recommended)
options.description: Parameterized queries + rescue email exceptions + unit tests for the critical paths.
